overview:
The chapter turns from lights and vessels to *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, the supernal man, and shows from a person why even its outer vessels are still the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*. "From my flesh I see G-d": man is a microcosm, with every nature and with a connection to G-d above them all. His *yechida* and *chaya* are in no vessel, yet his will shines through *chachma* and *bina* into the heart, all at one shot.

The heart is *lev*, thirty-two, because the thirty-two chambers of the brain, four brains of eight each, are revealed in it; in the mind they are the fifty gates of *bina*, still hidden in understanding. For an emotion to be born the intellect must first go away, like a rotting seed, through the narrow of the throat, and only the *uvchein* comes over. Yet the heart never diverges from the mind, so to change yourself, change your understanding. Down to the breath in the lungs it is still one with the will, as G-d's simple will is in the heart of *Zeir Anpin*. Along the way: an eighth of an eighth of *gaava*, and the Chanuka oil.

Like a person's body, which he controls and in which he feels his every desire, even its outer vessels still count as the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*.

blocks.text: Chapter 32: "Now we are going to talk about the heart." **Now**: now that the introduction about the lights and the vessels is finished, he starts to discuss why he wanted to tell us about the lights and the vessels. We have to understand the supernal man of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation), the man **that sits on the chair, the throne**. That is *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance) of *Atzilus*, which receives from the *Nehi* (*netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*) of *Abba* (*chachma* as a *partzuf*).

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text:
Having finished explaining *Abba*, he now starts to explain *Zeir Anpin*. Based on what was explained until now, *Zeir Anpin* is the *middos* (emotional attributes) of *Atzilus*, **the trunk and the root for the source of the source for the life of the worlds**: it all comes through *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*.

That is like the *mashal* (analogy) of the body: the body is where the soul is able to start affecting the world, once it comes into the body.

blocks.text: Nevertheless, **the body is still called the end of the world of the infinite**. It is still called an unlimited thing, a G-dly thing, **because G-d is one with the lights and with the vessels**, as was said before. Therefore, all the way to the external vessels of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, it is still called the world of the infinite.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text:
Just like in a person's body: even the most external vessels of his body can be controlled by him, so it is only a potential limitation. And not only that, his consciousness is revealed immediately in a feeling in his body. As soon as he has a desire, it is right away translated into a feeling in his lungs or something like that, an impulse to do something.

So as far as the *pnimiyus* (the inner side) goes, it is *mamash* (actually) one with him, with his consciousness; and as far as the *chitzoniyus* (the outer side) goes, he can control it to do whatever he wants. On both sides it is called infinite, still infinite. It is the intermediary between infinite and limited, but it is an infinite ability to limit things into however he wants.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: The lights and the vessels are finished. The reason they were explained now is that the main idea of the vessels is the vessels of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, and the *mashal* for those is the body. In a person, the soul is like the light and the body like the vessels. There is an idea of vessels in the soul itself even before it comes into the body, letters and different *hagbalos* (limitations), but the main thing is the body. That is what allows the consciousness of the soul to be in the body in a limited way, and also what allows the soul to interact with the world outside it: the two *inyanim* (matters) of the vessels, *kelim* and *tikunim*. So after that whole introduction about vessels, *gvul b'poel* and *gvul b'koach* (an actual limit and a limit in potential), he explains how it is in *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, all the way to its external vessels, is still called *Elokus* (G-dliness), the end of the world of the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite). The reason is that there is still a ray of the *Kav* (the line of light) there. The *mashal* is a person: your consciousness is felt in your body and your *ratzon* (will) is expressed in it. You control your body; it is a direct connection, and you can make it do whatever you want. Your body is limited, but it is only *gvul b'koach*: your hand can only move in certain ways, but within that field of motion you are unlimited. "It's *Ein Sof* within a very narrow, you know, field of movement and stuff, the little spectrum."

sections.title: From my flesh I see G-d: man is a microcosm, and his chaya and yechida are in no vessel
sections.summary: The body explains *Atzilus* because man was made in G-d's image: every level of creation is in him, and he also has a connection to G-d higher than all of them, the two things free choice needs. In the soul, *chaya* and *yechida* encompass the intellect and the emotions and are in no vessel; only from *chachma* down is the soul drawn into a vessel.

blocks.text: **To explain this**: "from my flesh I see G-d." From looking at the way our body works we will understand the way the vessels of *Atzilus* work, because **man was made in the image of G-d**. As it says, when G-d made man: "Let us make him **in our form, like our image**."

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Why does it say it in the plural? Because G-d was speaking to everything in creation, all the *sefiros* (the Divine attributes) and everything in the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent): every single level is put into man. Man is a microcosm of everything, and that is why it is in the plural. Rashi says it is because He said it also to the angels, and the angels are all the particular forms of the whole *hishtalshelus*. The reason is that man is a microcosm of everything: he has the whole world in him.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: It does not have to be that the way it is in you is the way it is upstairs, "but that's what it says in the Torah, that that's the way it is." That is first. Second, ultimately G-d did not have to do it that way; but the way our *hishtalshelus* is set up, according to the way our minds work and the way we understand things, if that is the way it is in you, that is the way it is upstairs. Because really you are a *chelek Elokah* (a part of G-d) that was given a form through *tzimtzumim* (contractions). So if you dig into yourself, you will uncover that G-dly essence, and you will see everything the way it is in G-d and the way it is everywhere.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: There is the depth: "if you reach into the depth, all of the wellsprings connect in the depth." But a person, in a revealed way, is *mamash* a microcosm of every form in the world. Every different type of animal and every different angel is in a person in a revealed way, unlike animals, which have only a certain nature.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: Penguins, hamsters and the black widow
blocks.text:
This is one of the two reasons why a person has free choice. To have free choice you need two things, and one thing a person has over animals is that he has all the different natures at his disposal. Every animal has a certain nature: some are naturally nice and some are naturally mean. The emperor penguins are naturally very respectful and caring of their babies, their eggs, and will do a lot for them. That is just their nature; they cannot help it. It is not that they decided to have this self-sacrifice: that is the way they are.

Other animals are very mean to their babies and eat their eggs. Some fish start to eat their eggs right after they lay them, and only the ones that survive are born. In some the father will eat the children if he is still there: "like Russian dwarf hamsters, I don't know, some of these kind of things or mice, I think." With some of these little animals, if there is a father you have to take him away from the kids; you cannot keep them in the same cage. Sometimes the mother is mean like that. The black widow spider is famous for eating her husband after they have kids. Some animals are faithful to their spouse and some are not, and some will even kill their spouse. There are all kinds of different natures.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: People have all of those at their disposal: the thing of being nice, the thing of being mean, all these different things, and you can choose whichever one you want. To have free choice you need that. But it is not good enough just to have the nature of everything. We also have the connection to G-d, which is higher than all the forms, and that is the other reason we have free choice: therefore we are able to choose whichever one we want. "You really need both." So a person has in him everything in creation, and also a connection to G-d which is higher than creation: he has everything in him.

blocks.text: "From my flesh I see G-d": man is made like an image of G-d, **for we see** **in the soul of man** that his *chaya* and *yechida* (the two highest levels of the soul), his inner volition and his self, encompass his intellect, emotions and actions, the consciousness on the levels of *nefesh*, *ruach* and *neshama*. These levels of the soul are higher than being in any particular vessel, any particular organ center.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: The *chaya* and *yechida* are the level of desire and of the simple essential pleasure of the *yechida*, and they are not in any particular vessel. So the inner desire and pleasure of the *yechida* is one thing. And there is also **the inner source of the intellect**, which is called *maskil* (one who has intellect): that is the *makif* (encompassing light) of *chaya*.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Both of these are **not limited to a specific vessel at all**. A person's inner self, which is expressed in desire and pleasure, his inner consciousness, and also his ability to have creative intellect, do not come from a vessel. They are just from the soul, spiritual things of the soul. The way they are expressed afterwards comes through the vessel of the body, as a biological, psychological thing that could be explained; but those levels themselves are not at all in a vessel, and they are not something that can be predetermined or manipulated on a physical level.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: *Chaya* is usually the thing of *ratzon*, but here he is putting it a little differently: *chaya* is the *pnimiyus* of the *sechel* (intellect), and *yechida* is the person's *ratzon v'taanug pashut*, his simple will and delight. There is a deeper level of *yechida* that is just the person himself: "That's the *yechida* without a name." The *yechida* with a name is the person's simple desire and pleasure, the *ratzon v'taanug ha'atzmi hapashut*: the pleasure of being himself, and the desire just to express himself, to be himself. Those are not limited in a vessel at all.

blocks.text: Then came the *nefesh*, *ruach*, *neshama*, *chaya* and *yechida*. The *chaya* and *yechida* are higher: they are not revealed in a certain organ center, but in a more general way, over the whole body. The *chaya* is the *koach hamaskil* (the power of insight), the inner ability for *chachma*, and the *yechida* is the *makif* of the *ratzon* and *taanug* (delight).

sections.title: Thirty-two paths of bina: why the heart is called lev
sections.summary: The brain has four parts, *chachma*, *bina*, and *daas* divided into *chesed* and *gevura*, and each has eight chambers: thirty-two, the thirty-two paths of *bina*. The heart, *lev* (thirty-two), is where they are revealed as emotion; in the mind they are the fifty gates of *bina*, still hidden in understanding like kindnesses covered within *Ima*, until they come out as love in the heart.

blocks.text: **The mind is divided into four parts.** Physically, too, the brain has four parts, and they correspond to the four parts of intellect. There is the cerebrum and the cerebellum. The cerebrum is in the front of the brain, the main thing, and behind it is a smaller brain, the cerebellum. The cerebrum is very apparently two hemispheres, what people call the right and the left brains, and the cerebellum is the back brain. The right and left brains correspond to *chachma* and *bina*, *chachma* on the right and *bina* on the left, and the cerebellum in the back corresponds to *daas* (knowledge), including the medulla oblongata: at the back of the cerebellum it turns into the spinal cord, and that part of the brain is the intermediary between the brain and the nerves in the body.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: The back brain, the cerebellum, is really also two brains. The brain of *daas* divides into two, *chesed* (kindness) and *gevura* (might, restraint), and physically it really is two hemispheres too. They are just attached much more tightly, so it looks like one, whereas the cerebrum looks like two, because its halves are separate and only attached by the thing in the middle.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text:
"Just for the record": all the middle stuff corresponds to *daas*. The thing that connects the right and left hemispheres of the cerebrum is part of the brain of *daas*; the whole back brain is the brain of *daas*; the medulla oblongata is the brain of *daas*; and the extensions from the middle brain to the eyes and ears and all the sensory organs are part of it: everything in the middle that connects. The medulla oblongata connects the intellect to the body, the cerebellum is the actual thinking of the *daas*, and there is the *daas elyon* (higher knowledge) that connects *chachma* and *bina*, with all the levels of *daas* we talk about.

Basically, the brain has four parts: the right and the left, and in the back two more, *chesed* and *gevura*. So there are *chachma* and *bina*, and then *daas* divides into *chesed* and *gevura*: four brains, four hemispheres, four chambers.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: וכל אחד יש בו ח' חדרים,
phrases.en: and each one of these four brains has eight chambers.

phrases.en: which is 32.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: And **each one of these four brains has eight chambers**: four times eight, **which is 32**. Each one has eight because each one has all four. Within *chachma* there is *chachma* of *chachma*, *bina* of *chachma*, *chesed* of *chachma* and *gevura* of *chachma*. And within each of those four there is the way it goes up and the way it goes down: the way you go into the theory, and the way you go to the application. It is like *chachma* and *Yisroel Saba*, and *bina* and *tevuna* (the sides of *chachma* and *bina* that go to the application).

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: The eight corners of a sukka
blocks.text: It is like a *sukka*, a cube: there are four corners on top and four corners on the bottom. The four corners on top correspond to the four letters of *Havaya*: *yud* is *chachma*, *hei* is *bina*, *vav* is *chesed*, and *hei* is *gevura*. The bottom corresponds to *alef*, *dalet*, *nun*, *yud*, the Name *Adnus*. That is the idea of the eight chambers in each of the brains, and eight times four is thirty-two: "so really you have 32 brains in your brain." Your brain is made up of thirty-two main brains, and each of those divides up more and more, infinitely.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Whenever you think something, you always have these thirty-two decisions going on. Say you get a new idea in *chachma*. It starts off as a flash in *chachma* of *chachma*, and then you have to send it: "this is like the way the brain works," it sends the electrical and chemical signals bouncing around from brain to brain. From the flash it goes right away to *bina*, and you start to think about it. Then it goes back and you have an emotion towards it, whether you like the idea or not, and you send it back to think about it more. Then it goes down to think of an application for it, and then back up to think more about the source, and it keeps bouncing around like that until it comes out as a particular train of thought with a particular idea.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: When you actually do it, it goes down your spine; but before you do it, to think about doing it, it has to go to the bottom part of the brain. There has to be *daas*, and there also has to be *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna*: a *chachma* for the practical and a *bina* for the practical. You have to have both, and then you can have a practical *chesed* and a practical *gevura*. You have all these things going on in your brain: eight chambers for each of the four brains, thirty-two.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: and this is why your heart is called a heart in Hebrew.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: because the source of the heart is in the 32 pathways of *bina*,

audio.lecture: 73 - Chap- 32-3 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

audio.lecture: 73 - Chap- 32-3 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: And **this is why your heart is called a heart in Hebrew**: the word *lev*, heart, has the numerical value of thirty-two, because the heart is the revelation of these thirty-two brains. That is what the heart is. Once your brain figures out what comes for each of these chambers, you experience a different emotion: the heart lets you feel each chamber. There are thirty-two main intellectual relationships you can have, and each one gives you a different emotional state. There are different ways to divide it up, but right now we are dividing it, in general, into thirty-two main emotional states.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: An eighth of an eighth of pride
blocks.text: "And this is by the way a very important, but slight digression": it says that a *talmid chacham* (a Torah scholar) has to have *shminis sheb'shminis*, an eighth of an eighth of *gaava* (haughtiness). An eighth of an eighth is a sixty-fourth. Why an eighth of an eighth? There are different explanations, but one of them relates to what we are talking about right now: your brain divides into thirty-two brains, and your heart is a revelation of those thirty-two, expressed in an emotional way.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text:
That is the *pnimiyus* of the heart: the inner part of the heart is actually called a brain too, because you understand things more fully when you experience them in your heart. Once you pick which chamber you want to experience, you stick it in your heart, and it lets you actually feel what it is like; you experience it as if it is a real thing, and so you understand it better. At that inner level your heart is actually a brain.

So you have sixty-four brains. And if you are a *talmid chacham*, one of those sixty-four brains has to be a brain of *gaava*. The other sixty-three have to be in a way of *anivus* (humility), of *bittul* (self-nullification); but one of them has to be in a way of *gaava*, of haughtiness.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Which one? "The top one." All of these brains are you understanding and interpreting the Torah, what the Torah said or what your *rebbe* taught you. But the point you start with, what the Torah said, has to be in a way of *gaava*: you have to say that is what it says, that is the truth, "and I'm not telling you my opinion." Your job should be just to teach, to explain and to interpret, but you should not feel that you have the jurisdiction to compromise in any way what the Torah says when you give it over. You can try to explain it to a person in a way he will understand.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text:
But say a person wants you to do something against the *Shulchan Aruch* (the Code of Jewish Law). Say somebody wants to convert, and it is not according to *halacha* (Jewish law), it is not proper. Or they say they did convert, but it was not a proper conversion, and now they want to marry somebody, "like it happens all the times." Reform, and Conservative especially, will twist things to the way people want to hear.

So if you feel that you are able to start to compromise on what the *Shulchan Aruch* says, or even if you are not going to actually convert somebody but just will not tell him the truth, if somebody asks you, "Am I Jewish according to *halacha*?" or "Am I allowed to do this according to *halacha*?" and you do not want to tell him the truth, you try to make it sound different and tell him something that is not true, then you are not really teaching the Torah. You are telling him your own ideas, twisting it to what he wants to hear. You are not just giving over the Torah, and so you are not a *talmid chacham* anymore.

blocks.text: That is the *chachma* of *chachma*, the thirty-second one. The thirty-second path corresponds to the *shaar hanun* (the fiftieth gate): the level of the *etzem* (essence), where it connects to the thing itself. Everything else is just interpretation; there is the thing itself, the fact, and everything else is an explanation of the fact. It is just the *pshat* (the plain meaning), real straight: that is what it says and that is what it means, that is it. "Now I'm going to explain it to you, but you have to start off always with that premise." That has to be first, before you start explaining anything.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's advice before a debate
blocks.text:
The Rebbe told Rabbi Hollander, "he came and spoke for us once", who was going to debate with Reform and Conservative rabbis. He did not even want to debate with them, because he did not want to give them credence, to make it look as if they were legitimate rabbis who represent Judaism: "I'm one form of Judaism, they're another form of Judaism." He wanted to make it clear that if you do not follow what it says in the *Shulchan Aruch*, then it is not Judaism.

So the Rebbe told him that the first thing he should say is something to the effect of: "I do not view you as a rabbi, and I do not recognize what you say, and I don't agree with your whole religion." Start off by saying that you totally do not agree with them and do not give them any credence as rabbis.

blocks.title: They make the compromises holy
blocks.text:
That is also what the Rebbe said when they asked him what the problem is with Reform and Conservative: "everybody makes compromises, but they make the compromises holy." You have to say that whatever it says in the *Shulchan Aruch* is the truth, and that is what everyone has to do.

Now, you could say: you are not at the level to do everything, you are not ready to do everything in the *Shulchan Aruch*, so start with this: drive to *shul* on *Shabbos*. "Drive, but come to shul at least." That is a compromise: you are telling him to start, not to do everything at once, and you are supposed to do that; you are supposed to start slow. But you cannot say that that is actually what G-d wants, that G-d wants you to be just like that, that it is good and you do not have to do anything else, that this is the goal.

blocks.text: So this is the idea of the heart, called thirty-two because the thirty-two brains are revealed in it. Its source is in the thirty-two pathways of *bina*, **which are these 32 chambers of the brain**.

blocks.text: Then he started to explain how it goes from the mind to the heart. The mind has four parts: the two brains in the front, *chachma* and *bina*, the two hemispheres of the cerebrum; and the back brain, the brain of *daas*, the cerebellum, which has two parts too. It looks more like one brain, but if you look carefully it is also two hemispheres, closely attached. That is the *chesed* and *gevura* in the *daas*: when you connect to an idea you can say it is good or bad. Each of those has eight, like a *sukka*, because each has the four, *chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura*, and then the way they go up into the abstract, theoretical side of the idea and the way they go down to the practical, as chapters one and two explained about *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna*, the difference between *bina* and *tevuna*. So each of the four brains has eight; eight times four is thirty-two, the thirty-two paths of *bina*.

That gives you a certain emotion, a certain feeling, which is the way your body knows how to react to what you are understanding. blocks.title: A path through the woods
blocks.text:
And the *shvilin*, the pathways, are the way it breaks through. As it says of the Red Sea, when it was split it was made into twelve *shvilin*; "you know, like when the Rebbe would come through 770 and make a *shvil*." A *shvil* breaks through something; it is not a road. What is the difference between a *derech* (a way) and a *shvil*? A *shvil* is like a path in the woods, where there is grass and trees and bushes and you cannot go through any other way: you have to go through this little break.

Normally the brain will not connect to the emotions. But through these thirty-two paths, which are like the idea of the *uvchein* ("and so": the conclusion that applies the idea to me), it comes across into the heart, and you are able to feel it. That is why it is called *lev*.

blocks.title: Money in an economics class and in a get-rich-quick tape
blocks.text: For example, say a person is thinking about money. There are two different ways you could think about money. You could think about it in an economics class, where the fact that it is good and that you want it is covered over, because you are just dealing with the intellectual aspect of it, how it works. Or you can think about it in a get-rich-quick tape, where you are thinking about what you can do with it, and it relates more to an emotion. In the class there is a recognition that money is a good thing and people want it, which is the whole basis of the economic system and why you are discussing it, but you are not thinking about it in a way that relates to your emotions. Or like in law.

blocks.title: The disinterested law student
blocks.text: When you study law, you try to be disinterested, not uninterested. If you are going to be successful in the class you should be interested, but disinterested: you should not feel an emotional connection to the outcome of the case. You should be objective, impartial. To do that you have to view the thing as an intellectual issue. What is really going on? What are the issues at hand? What is the real meaning of the term when we say ownership, property, liability? Where do they extend to? How does it apply? You think of it all in abstract, intellectual terms, and even though you could come to the conclusion that something is good or bad, that somebody is guilty, it is a little removed from an emotion. Translate it to a practical case, especially one that is relevant to you, "Well, that means that you don't really own your house," and then you will get emotional about it. That is different.

It does not have to be a positive excitement, just some sort of response. It does not even have to be emotional: *hispaalus* does not imply emotions. It is that concept, but it could be an intellectual thing; it is any sort of effect the thing has on you.

blocks.text: **So too, the 32 pathways of the mind are revealed from the hidden excitement that's in the mind, and they're revealed in the heart.** That is why the heart is called *lev*. As it says in *Etz Chaim* (the Arizal's Tree of Life): **why is it called the heart**? Because the thirty-two lights of *Abba* collect there, the thirty-two paths. These are the thirty-two times that, in the story of creation in *Bereishis*, it says *vayomer Elokim*, "and G-d said", with the name *Elokim*, which represents *bina*, which receives from *chachma*, the lights of *Abba*. **Like it's explained elsewhere at length**.

blocks.text:
In a person, all the different excitements and feelings in his heart, with all their shades of good and bad and in between, and the way he feels like acting based on them, all come from the mind. The mind is connected to his consciousness, and it is all based on his inner desire, on what he wants. It is all *mamash* coming from his *yechida* straight into what he feels in his heart.

So too with the way G-d runs the world. Whatever relationship is revealed, the different emotions, are all expressions of G-d's choice: He is choosing to reveal Himself in that way. It goes from G-d's inner desire to reveal Himself, through the intellect, the certain way He chooses to reveal Himself, and based on that He assumes different relationships with the world, to express Himself in different ways.

audio.lecture: 73 - Chap- 32-3 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Then the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for). When the mind and the heart connect, the awareness of G-dliness comes out into the way we act: the way we react to and feel about the world is influenced by our understanding of G-dliness. "And so we're not afraid of anything except for G-d, and we don't love anything except for G-d." So when something happens, we are able to pass the *nisayon* (the test), because we recognize that the only thing that is important and really a factor is what G-d wants; everything else is irrelevant. When a person acts that way, that is the *nimshal* in the *avoda* (divine service).

blocks.text: Then the real *nimshal* happens: we fulfill the purpose of the world, which is the brain, making an awareness of G-dliness, the *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below) for which G-d is making the world. That automatically makes the heart correspond: the *middos*, *midda k'neged midda* (measure for measure), the way G-d relates to us, are also that way. G-d does miracles for us and answers our prayers, because it is revealed how the heart is connected to the brain: it is apparent how our connection to G-d influences our daily life, that He does things for us.

blocks.text: Really it is always like that: the way G-d conducts the world is based on the *sechel*, the intellect, so if the *sechel* changes, automatically the *midda* will change. But for that connection to be revealed there has to be a certain maturity, which will be explained soon: the different levels of maturity of *Zeir Anpin*, whether it has *gadlus hamochin* or *katnus hamochin* (mature or immature intellect). The *sechel* changes based on us. There is a certain *ratzon* which stays the same, and the *sechel* tells the *ratzon* how to accomplish what it wants; that depends on the situation.

audio.lecture: 74 - Chap- 32-4 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: And there is the *chitzoniyus* of the *mochin* and the *pnimiyus hamochin*. The *chitzoniyus hamochin* is that G-d has the world set up in a certain way, the source of *teva* (nature), and it just runs that way because G-d wants the world to be a certain way: so that it should exist, and also so that we should have the challenge of *Torah* and *mitzvos*. But when we reveal our *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice) for G-d and for *Torah* and *mitzvos*, and connect to them in a deeper way, even in an external way but mainly when it is done with *mesirus nefesh*, then we connect to the *pnimiyus hamochin*. And when you connect to the *pnimiyus hamochin*, G-d will change the *teva* for you, "because then you're going to the reason before the system."

audio.lecture: 74 - Chap- 32-4 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: The Chanuka oil
blocks.text: That is like the miracle of Chanuka. The *Yidden* (the Jews) had *mesirus nefesh* to do a *mitzva b'hiddur* (a commandment in the finest way). They did not need *mesirus nefesh* to light the *menora*: they could have used the impure oil; *halachically* they would have been allowed to. But they wanted to have *mesirus nefesh* to do the *mitzva b'hiddur*. They could have saved some of the oil for the later days, but they did not want to. They wanted not to compromise at all, to do the *mitzva* the best way today, and they trusted in G-d for the rest of the days: "that's His problem."

audio.lecture: 74 - Chap- 32-4 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 74 ends its review of the thirty-two paths (lines 16-27) with their nimshal and mesirus nefesh; placed under the last passage on the paths.

blocks.text: When a person has that type of attitude, that the whole purpose of the world is for us to serve G-d, and we are going to have *mesirus nefesh* in *gashmiyus* and *ruchniyus* (physical and spiritual things) to do things in the best way, because we recognize that G-d is creating the world and runs everything, and the whole reason the world is here is for us to do this, so it has to help us; when a person acts in a way that expresses that understanding, even if he does not understand it so much, since the main thing is the action, then G-d, *midda k'neged midda*, will reveal that connection with open miracles, like the Chanuka miracle.

audio.lecture: 74 - Chap- 32-4 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 74 ends its review of the thirty-two paths (lines 16-27) with their nimshal and mesirus nefesh; placed under the last passage on the paths.

blocks.text:
*Mesirus nefesh* means making it the top priority. If a person says, "Well, we have the oil anyway, so we'll use it," that is not *mesirus nefesh*. *Mesira* means that you are giving yourself over: you dedicate yourself, "I'm committing to do this no matter what." "Simple words, you know, no romanticism." It is your top priority. If anything comes up, big or little: I commit that I am going to put on *tefillin*. It is going to cost me money? I don't care. It is going to take time? I don't care. Somebody is going to want to kill me? I don't care. Somebody is going to say I am being *mevatel* (wasting) time from Torah? I don't care.

*Mesirus nefesh* does not have to be for a good thing; you can have *mesirus nefesh* for a bad thing. It just means that you give yourself over to the thing, committing to do it as your top priority, so that everything else is secondary, and if anything else contradicts it, big or small, you will not consider the other thing of any importance.

blocks.text: A person's *mesirus nefesh* should not be for the *mitzva* per se, as its own *inyan*. But when a person recognizes that every *mitzva* is connected to G-d's *etzem* (essence), and he has *mesirus nefesh* for G-d, then if G-d tells him to do this, he says: okay, so it must be that I can do this *mitzva*, and it is impossible for anything to stand in my way.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: The Alter Rebbe in jail
blocks.text:
That applies even to a *ruchniyus* thing. When the Alter Rebbe was in jail, they told him, "You have to eat, or else you'll be killing yourself": he would die and lose both this world and the next, his *olam haba*, because it would be suicide not to eat the non-kosher food. It is true that *al pi Torah* (according to the Torah) you could get a *heter* (permission) in that situation to eat the non-kosher food. But if you believe that the whole reason the world is here is to do *Torah* and *mitzvos*, and that this is the *teva* of the world, you are allowed to expect a miracle when you are trying to do a *mitzva*.

Besides, there are opinions that say you are allowed to; and "that's not such an example": it is not certain that he would die right away, it is not immediate danger, and even halachically it is not such a big question. But if a person has such an attitude, as the Rebbe said about the Frierdiker Rebbe, "you know you're going to win."

Even for a positive *mitzva*, you can always find a source for these things in *halacha*, because the whole thing of *halacha* is to tell you how to be a person with this attitude. The Torah wants you to be a person who lives in the world with a certain attitude, *Elokus bifshitus v'ha'olam b'hischadshus* (G-dliness as a simple fact, and the world as the novelty). All the particular laws are advice and ways to get yourself to be like that, to show what it means to be such a person.

One of the things is that nothing in *gashmiyus* can stop you from doing a *mitzva*. And another big rule is that nothing in *kedusha* (holiness) can contradict another thing in *kedusha*. If a person thinks that one *mitzva*, or one *inyan* in *kedusha*, is going to prevent or lessen his ability to do some other thing in *kedusha*, he is making a mistake somewhere: either it is not really a thing in *kedusha*, or he is mistaken that it will mess him up.

sections.title: The intellect must go away before the emotion: the rotting seed and the narrow of the throat
sections.summary: An emotion that is only implicit in understanding can be born in the heart only after a *tzimtzum* and a *histalkus*: the intellect has to go away, as a seed rots before it grows. That is the *meitzar hagaron*, the narrow of the throat between brain and heart, one of three partitions in the body, with the membrane over the brain and the diaphragm.

phrases.en: Before you can have the emotion, you have to first have a *tzimtzum*, a *helem* and a *kibutz*: the idea has to be focused down to a *uvchein*, the *sechel* has to be hidden, and the light has to be removed. This is called a *histalkus*.

blocks.text: And behold, **surely when the emotion has to be created**, when you actually want to feel something in your heart, where is it going to come from? From the hidden excitement of the *midda* (attribute), the way it is in your intellect and the understanding of *bina*. Implicit in your understanding is a certain *midda* already: you understood intellectually that this thing is bad for you, but you did not necessarily feel it yet.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: Would you turn on the light for me on Shabbos?
blocks.text:
A person learns *halacha*: implicit in that *halacha* is that in such and such a situation this thing would be *assur* (forbidden), but he did not necessarily think about it. He learns that if somebody does this, they stone him; or he learns *hilchos Shabbos*: this is an *issur d'oraisa* (a Torah prohibition), this is an *issur d'rabbanan* (a rabbinic one), this is *mutar* (allowed), this is *patur* (exempt). While he is learning all those things there is an implicit *midda*, not revealed right now, that this thing is bad and he would be scared to do it, especially in the time of the *beis din* (the court), when a person would get *skila* (stoning) for it, because it is against what G-d wants.

But since he understands that it is against *halacha*, that *midda* will automatically come out if somebody says, "Dude, would you turn the light on for me on *Shabbos*?" He would be very scared to do it; he would not do it. Even something little, *muktza* (what may not be moved on *Shabbos*), a *d'rabbanan*: he learned about it, so he would not do it. "You want to hand me that stone?" "No, it's *muktza*."

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: So **before you can have the emotion, you have to first have a** *tzimtzum* (contraction), a *helem* (concealment) and a *kibutz* (gathering): the idea has to be focused down to a *uvchein*, the *sechel* has to be hidden, and the light has to be removed. This is called a *histalkus* (departure): the *sechel* has to go away.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Like the *mashal* of the rotting of a seed: **in order to change from one thing to another**, from physical to spiritual, it has to rot. The original thing has to go away for the new thing to come out, because the original thing contradicts the new thing. So if a person is focused on the intellect, and that is his interest, the emotion will not be able to come out. Therefore the intellect has to go away for him to really feel the emotion.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: "This is one of the reasons why women get more emotional, because they're *kalei daas*" (of light mind). And little children are more emotional, while somebody who is more mature, especially a *bar sechel*, a real intellectual person, has emotions that are always very subdued and cold, because he is always thinking of things intellectually.

blocks.text: As long as a person is focusing on the intellectual aspect, the emotions are going to be quiet; and when a person is being very emotional, he is not being rational. But this is only in *chitzoniyus*, because this is a *chitzoniyus'dik sechel*, an outer intellect. With a *pnimiyus'dik sechel*, an inner one, they can both come together. "That's the rule for anything": any division between things is only in *chitzoniyus*; if you go deep enough, they connect. This is a *klal gadol* (a great rule): whenever you learn in *Chassidus* that two things are different and contradict, one higher and one lower, if you go deep enough there is a level where they connect.

blocks.text: So: **this is the idea of the narrow of the throat**, the *meitzar hagaron*. From your brain to your heart you have to go through the neck, and the neck is narrow: physically it represents that it has to be focused and channeled, to get smaller. And it is also the idea that the brain stops.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: This also has to do with this week's, last week's, *parsha* (Torah portion). In the throat there are the *kaneh*, the *veshet* and the *veridin*: the windpipe, the esophagus or food pipe, and the jugular vein. Those three *simanim* (signs), as in the *shechita* (ritual slaughter) of an animal, correspond to the three powers, the three officers: the *sar hamashkim*, the *sar ha'ofim* and the *sar hatabachim* (the chief butler, the chief baker and the chief of the slaughterers). "So, that's just a little living with the time there."

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: **When it goes into the narrow of the throat of** *bina*, **the excitement of the intellect goes away**, and then it is changed and becomes an emotional excitement in the heart. In the mind you are excited about the intellect of it; when it goes into the heart, you are excited in an emotional way, by the *uvchein*, not by the actual understanding.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: Tell me why I should care
blocks.text: In the mind there is the whole thing of how beautiful the idea is, how great the explanations were. A person goes to a good *shiur* (class), and if he really enjoyed it he is excited, mainly by how well it was explained, that he understood an idea he did not understand before: that is the intellectual aspect. Then some people do not care about intellect so much, and they say, "Okay, but why do I care? It was very nice, you explained all this stuff, but who cares? Tell me why I should care." That is the heart speaking. The heart wants to know how it relates to me in a personal way. The intellect does not care about a personal way; it just wants to know things, just to know. But your heart wants to know how it should relate to it, which means you have to know how you fit in the picture. That is the *uvchein*.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: Is G-d giving me money, or the stock market?
blocks.text: So the *sechel* has to go away, and you have to feel only the *uvchein*: "Oh, based on what he said..." Like in a *beis din*: the man wants to know whether it is his money or not. He does not want to know the reasoning; just, is it your money or his money? The same with this. You learn this whole thing in *Chassidus*, and your heart wants to know, "Okay, so at the end of the day, is G-d giving me money or is the stock market giving me money? Should I be afraid of it? How should I react differently to the world based on this explanation?" This is the idea of a *memutza* (a middle) or a *masach* (a screen).

blocks.text:
**This is similar to the** *kruma d'avira* (the membrane of air). There are three *parsaos* (partitions) in the body, which separate between the *Chabad*, the *Chagas* (*chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*) and the *Nehi*. From the *koach hamaskil* to the brain there is the *kruma d'avira*, the membrane of air over the brain, which takes the liquid from the *koach hamaskil* and the *taanug* and brings it into the brain in a way of *hevel* (vapor). Then there is the *meitzar hagaron*, which goes from the *sechel* to the *middos* and changes a *sechel* into a *midda* by letting only the *uvchein* come over. Then there is the *chatzar hakaved*, the diaphragm between your heart and lungs and the digestive organs, the liver and the stomach, which brings an emotion to a physical impulse, getting you ready to react physically to the emotion, to run away or to do something.

So **the membrane of air** separates between the *koach hamaskil*, which is higher than intellect, and the brain, and changes it so that it comes into the brain as an idea, as a *sechel*.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text:
And like the *chatzar hakaved* (lit. the partition of the liver), which is the diaphragm, the muscle underneath the lungs: it separates between the organs of breathing, the cardiovascular system, and the organs of digestion, the digestive system, **so that it should change from an emotion to a physical thing**.

So if a person is scared, he will have to go to the bathroom. Why? Because the emotion changes the way you are breathing, and that change in the rhythm of your diaphragm pushes on your stomach differently, and it also triggers different things that get your digestive system to kind of shut off and empty itself, so that you will be able to run away better: you will not waste energy digesting food, and you do not want the weight of the food. In general, a person's digestion is affected by how fast he is breathing. As explained elsewhere at length.

sections.title: The heart follows the mind exactly, all the way to the breath of the chest
sections.summary: Though the emotion changes its nature, it never diverges from the understanding: the heart needs the mind to tell it where to go, so the way to change yourself is to change your understanding. The emotion is a whole *partzuf*, its thought, its feeling and its reflex, and even its outer vessel, the breath in the lungs, is still one with the will: still *Ein Sof*.

Your heart is never going to run away and go off on its own, because it does not know where to go. It needs your mind to tell it where to go. Once the mind tells it, it goes and runs with it farther than the mind would have gone. Once your mind says it is a good thing, the heart says, "All right, it's a good thing, all the way good," and it runs: "That's it, I love it, I'm going to go do it." And the mind says, "Oh, wait a minute, wait a minute," but the heart says, "Too late, you already told me it's good, I'm going." So if your mind tells your heart that a thing is good, your heart can get excited even in a way that is irrational, but it is never going to have an emotion that is different from your understanding.

blocks.text: That is one of the basic premises of *Chabad Chassidus*: since *mo'ach shalit al halev*, your mind controls the heart, and your actions are according to your emotions, you should go to the root of the problem and change your understanding. If you change the way you understand things, automatically you will change the way you feel towards them, and automatically you will change the way you act towards them. As the last chapter explained, there is **the intellect of the emotion, the feeling of the emotion, and the natural impulse or reflex of the emotion**: the way it sinks in, the effect it has on you. These are the *muskal*, the *murgash* (the felt) and the *mutba* (the impressed, the reflex).

blocks.title: Somebody punches you
blocks.text: The *muskal* of it is that you are thinking why you are excited. Somebody punches you: "Oh, he punched me, I'm so..." Then there is the feeling of it: you get all hot, "like you breathe fire from your nose", your breathing gets heavy and quicker, you take deep breaths, your heart starts pumping, your blood is boiling, you turn red. And the *mutba* is the reflex, the physical change it makes in your body: your muscles tense up, and that is part of how you feel it. The feeling of being angry comes along with physical changes that get your body ready to run away or to fight with somebody.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: "I mean really it's like getting... it's really gets a person ready to kill somebody. That's really what it is." Nowadays it is usually tamer, and people are usually not in these kinds of situations, but the emotion is really for the extreme: if this guy is dangerous and is going to hurt you, you have to get rid of him. That is what it is trying to get you ready to do. With fear you would run away; with anger, you want to kill the person. "Maybe it doesn't come out that far because you don't want to get arrested or whatever, but really that's what the emotion wants to do."

blocks.text: **But even the external vessels of the** *Nehi* **of the heart**. It was explained that the *Chabad* of the emotion goes into the right side of the heart, the *Chagas* of the emotion into the left side, and the *Nehi* is in the lungs. So even the external vessel of the *Nehi* of the heart, the excitement of the heart when it comes, like a *chesed* and love, to the outside, in the *Nehi* of the chest, of the lungs, **in thought, speech and action**. What does that mean? Your lungs now become a vessel to make you think, speak and do.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: The most obvious is speaking: the emotion is expressed in your voice; you hear the emotion in the voice. But your thought also gets a certain emotional background from the feeling it gets from how fast you are breathing. That changes different things in your body, oxygen levels, whatever, and that is how you know what emotion goes along with what you are thinking: "you can have different tones of voice within your own thoughts, also." How fast you breathe sets the rhythm: when you are breathing fast you think faster, and it makes a rushed feeling. And then there is action. When a person is happy, he does things in a light, relaxed way, kind of bouncy; when he is angry he is tense and jerky. That comes mainly from the change in your lungs, how fast you are breathing.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text:
This is through the external vessel of the heart, which is the lungs: the *mutba*, the thing that makes the emotion sink in, the reflex of the emotion, which is in the *hevel hachaze* (the breath of the chest) of *Zeir Anpin*. In your breathing there is a change based on your emotions. About this it says, *ihu v'garmohi chad* (He and His organs are one): the emotion makes an effect all the way to the outer vessel of the *Nehi* of *Zeir Anpin*, and that comes directly from your intellect, which comes directly from your *ratzon* and *taanug*. Whatever your will and delight are, they are felt in your lungs, in how you are breathing, and so you feel different emotions. The day-to-day of how you feel, what mood you are in, how tense you are, is all affected. In that way it is connected all the way back to your *ratzon*: "So it's *mamash* one."

It is all still *Ein Sof*, in its own way: like in the *mashal*, it is still **under your control**; you are still a *ba'al bechira* (one with free choice) to control it.

sections.title: The mashal and the nimshal: the will felt in the heart, and G-d's simple will in the heart of Zeir Anpin
sections.summary: In a person the essential will shines through the intellect into the heart and is felt in the breath of the chest: the *re'usa d'liba*, the heart's yearning for good, one with the will at one shot. So too in *Zeir Anpin*, the heart of G-d's conduct of the world: whether *vayomer el libo* or *vayisatzev el libo*, it is G-d's simple will from before the *tzimtzum*, and so all of it is still the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*.

It does not mean that whatever you feel you should do. blocks.text: There was a thing with the Rebbe Rashab: he washed his hands a certain way, three times or something on each hand, and somebody asked him why he did that. He said, "I don't know why, but I trained my body to always follow *Shulchan Aruch* exactly, and so I know that if my body does it that way, then that's the way you're supposed to do it. There must be a reason." That is, in a way, even more than what we are talking about here.

But he still has this inner yearning. Ever since he was a little kid he always had this thing: he wanted to be a good, holy guy, like Moshe and Avraham. blocks.text: So all the way to the end of the vessels of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, it is still called the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*. The revelation of the way G-d conducts the world, whether He gives or does not give *hashpaa* (flow), money and food and all these kinds of things, is still called the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*: it is still controlled by G-d, and it is still revealed that it is controlled by Him.

audio.lecture: 77 - Chap- 32-7 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA  (End).mp3

blocks.text: That is **because He and His organs are one**, **just like in the person**: a person's inner *ratzon* and his heart are like one *mahus* (what a thing is in itself). They are connected totally, and the one expresses the other exactly, both from up to down and from down to up: the *ratzon* goes into the heart, and the feeling of the heart goes all the way up to the inner *ratzon*.

reviewQuestions.question: Why are even the external vessels of *Zeir Anpin* still called the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*, and what does a person's body show about it?
What two things does a person have that give him free choice, and how do the animals' natures show the first?
How do four brains with eight chambers each make thirty-two, and why is the heart called *lev*?
Why must the intellect go away before the emotion is felt in the heart, and what do the rotting seed and the *meitzar hagaron* show?
If the emotion changes its nature, why is the best way to change yourself to change your understanding?
What is the *re'usa d'liba*, and how does it show that the heart and the essential will are one?

notes.text: Line 4 repeats the word sof ("sof olam ha'Ein Sof"), so it cannot be cut where he pauses after it: its first phrase runs to "chad" and cites his English for the whole clause (71 w233-276), which has his reading of "mishum d'ihu v'chayohi v'garmohi chad" inside it.

Phrases he reads without translating keep their Hebrew alone: the second half of line 17 (the four mochin), the closing "v'chayadua" of line 29 and "kayadua" of line 33, "v'cha'hai gavna" in line 46, the second half of line 47 (he explains it instead, 77 w998-1097), and "v'dai l'mevin" in line 50. The first phrase of line 12 cites his paraphrase right after his reading (71 w1872-1899), and line 47's first phrase cites his gloss of the external vessel.

Line 28: he reads "tzimtzum v'helem v'kibutz" (75 w1131-1140) where the chapter has "v'kivutz" (contraction); the phrase and the block keep his *kibutz*. Line 26: he reads only "orois d'Abba", not "v'Ima". Line 16: he reads "l'ZuN" where the text has "l'Zeir Anpin"; his English ("the brains, the intellect for the emotions") is kept without the letters.
Line 29: the transcript has him say the seed rots "in order to change from physical to spiritual" (75 w1231-1238); kept as transcribed, though it may be misheard.

Line 45: he takes "vayomer el libo" as "talking about the Mabul", as G-d deciding in His heart to make a flood. The verse (Bereishis 8:21) is G-d's resolve after the Flood never again to destroy, which fits the line's "l'hatos l'chesed"; "vayisatzev el libo" (Bereishis 6:6) is before it. Kept as he said it.

Class 74 is a review of classes 71-73 (lines 1-27), then the nimshal of the thirty-two paths and mesirus nefesh, which class 75 finishes before it reads line 28. The alignment marks line 17 in it (74 w816, confidence 0.53); its blocks are placed by what they review, each with outOfPlace: lines 4-5, 13-15, 19, and 25-27.

Sensitivity: six blocks are flagged. Three in class 72 on the Reform and Conservative movements (other-groups): the conversion aside, the Rebbe's advice to Rabbi Hollander before a debate, and "they make the compromises holy". The Alter Rebbe in jail (75 w343-548, health-or-legal: "you are allowed to expect a miracle" rather than eat forbidden food). Women as kalei daas (75 w1311-1368, women). The hurricanes beside the Flood (77 w783-915, other). Left unflagged as ordinary Torah positions or humor: "he goes back to being a regular stupid person" about a scholar without gaava, anger "gets a person ready to kill somebody", the frightened person who has to go to the bathroom, and "scientists can't figure out how the world works... because it's not a system" (a claim about science, not a jab at a group, unlike the one flagged in chapter 30). A reviewer may want to look at the drive-to-shul-on-Shabbos example (72 w2602-2648), kept in the publishable text because it is the point of the story.
Rabbi Hollander (72 w2241): named as having spoken for them once; who he is is not said. "The Rebbe said about the Frierdiker Rebbe" (75 w511-548) is given without the saying itself.

Line 30: "living with the time" (75 w1639-1648) is the Chabad phrase for living with the weekly Torah portion; the three officers are those of Pharaoh in Vayeshev, which he connects to the three simanim of the throat.
